PDF Search
==========
A small Mac app for searching, reading, annotating and citing your research PDFs.
Search every word of every PDF, write notes in the margins, copy citations.

Requires macOS 13 (Ventura) or later. Runs on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.


INSTALL
-------
1. Drag "PDF Search" onto the Applications folder in this window.

2. Open it from Applications. The first time, macOS will warn that it can't verify the
   app (it isn't from the App Store or a registered Apple developer). To allow it:

   macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later:
     - Click "Done" on the warning (NOT "Move to Trash").
     - Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down to the message
       "PDF Search was blocked...", click "Open Anyway", and enter your password.
     - Open PDF Search again and click "Open".

   macOS 13-14:
     - Right-click (or Control-click) PDF Search in Applications, choose Open, then Open again.

   You only have to do this once.

   (Terminal alternative:  xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/PDF Search.app")


GET STARTED
-----------
- Put your PDFs in a folder called "Papers" in your home folder (your own papers in Papers/Library).
  PDF Search reads every PDF once (a progress bar shows how far it's got); after that, searches
  are instant. You can also drag any folder of PDFs into the window.
- Type words in the search box. Click a result to see the PDF with the matches marked.
- Select a passage and press H to highlight it. Type a note in the box that appears beside it.
- Your bibliography is a plain library.bib file in the Papers folder (or your Obsidian vault,
  if you have one). Shift-Command-C copies a citation for the open paper.
- The full guide is in Extras > "PDF Search Guide.pdf".

Your PDFs stay where they are. PDF Search never moves or copies them. It only changes a PDF
when you highlight text or write a margin note in it (saved into the file, like in Preview).


WHAT'S IN EXTRAS
----------------
- PDF Search Guide.pdf: how everything works
- Source Code: the complete app (one Swift file), so you can build or change it yourself,
  plus a tool for moving a Zotero library into PDF Search
